title: ECCB Prudential Standard on Climate-Related and Environmental Risks for Institutions Licensed Under the Banking Act, 2015
citation: Eastern Caribbean Central Bank, Prudential Standard on Climate-Related and Environmental Risks for Institutions Licensed under the Banking Act, 2015 (cover dated August 2023), issued under s. 184 of the Banking (Amendment) Act, 2015
evidence: No official ECCB page could be opened (https://www.eccb-centralbank.org/enforced and /standards answer 403 to curl and to headless Chromium from the cloud address on 2026-11-03), so no official page states the date and in_force is null. Section 1.0 of the standard, read in a copy hosted by SBF Network (https://data.sbfnetwork.org/sites/default/files/survey-attachments/2025-05/2024-07-30-11-23-57-Prudential-Standard-on-Climate-related-and-Environmental-Risks.pdf, 200, 294880 bytes, 2026-11-03), says: "This Prudential Standard shall come into effect on the 1st day of March, 2024." A search of eccb-centralbank.org lists the standard by this title on the Enforced page.
notes: Regional instrument, link only: the ECCB serves it for every institution licensed under the Banking Act, 2015 in the ECCU, so the same instrument sits in the scope of AG, DM, KN, LC, VC and the territories AI and MS. The existing register row carried law_family F6; it is mapped to F1 here (board oversight, risk management, stress testing, disclosure s. 5.5 and reporting s. 5.6). The brief asked for the standard's own PDF page as official_url: the ECCB site refuses the cloud address, no ECCB PDF address was found, so official_url stays the Enforced page the existing row already pointed to. verification is official_page_seen from the earlier session's archived copy of that page, not from this one. No text is stored.

title: Physical Planning and Development Control Act, 2016 (Act No. 23 of 2016)
citation: Physical Planning and Development Control Act, 2016 (Act No. 23 of 2016), assented 26 July 2016, commenced by S.R.O. 39 of 2016
evidence: S.R.O. 39 of 2016, Physical Planning and Development Control Act (Commencement) Notice, 2016, para 2 (gazetted 29 July 2016): "The Physical Planning and Development Control Act No. 23 of 2016, shall come into force on the 1st day of August, 2016." Opened https://grenadaparliament.gd/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/S.R.O.-39-of-2016-Physical-Planning-and-Development-Control-Act-Commencement-Notice-2016.pdf (200, 53749 bytes) on 2026-11-03.
notes: Used as the act carrying environmental duties: no Environment Act is in force in Grenada (an Environment Bill is on the 2025/26 legislative agenda, not an official-page statement read in this session). The Act is a planning and development-control statute; its environmental content includes the duty to protect the natural and cultural heritage (long title) and environmental impact assessment in the permission process (s. 22(4)(g), as amended by gd-ppdca-amendment-2017). It repeals and replaces the Physical Planning and Development Control Act, Cap. 241A (Act No. 25 of 2002), which is not stored. The record is the Act as passed, dated its commencement; the Parliament site serves no consolidation. Subsidiary instruments are not in scope: S.R.O. 42 of 2016 adopts the OECS Building Code (a 5 MB schedule) and S.R.O. 36 of 2017 is a project-specific order. Language stored on 2026-11-03: en (English is the official language of legislation; the Parliament site serves no other language and no translation).

title: Physical Planning and Development Control (Amendment) Act, 2017 (Act No. 23 of 2017)

The Act has no commencement clause (section 1 is the short title only); the 2016 principal Act carries "[ By Notice ]" in the same place, so the bracketed date is read as the commencement date. Opened https://grenadaparliament.gd/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Act-23-of-2017-Physical-Planning-and-Development-Control-Amendment.pdf (200, 377393 bytes) on 2026-11-03.
notes: Amends gd-ppdca-2016: ss. 2, 6, 22(4)(g) (inserts "Impact" so the paragraph reads Environmental Impact), 39(3)(d) (a Ministry of the Environment representative) and Schedule I. No consolidated text is served by the Parliament site, so the amendment is stored as its own record. The date is the one the official text prints; no gazette commencement notice was found. title: Consumer Protection Act, 2018 (Act No. 2 of 2018)
citation: Consumer Protection Act, 2018 (Act No. 2 of 2018), assented 18 January 2018, commenced by S.R.O. 44 of 2020; amended by Act No. 5 of 2020
evidence: S.R.O. 44 of 2020, Consumer Protection Act (Commencement) Order, 2020, para 2 (gazetted 26 June 2020): "The Consumer Protection Act No. 2 of 2018 shall come into force on the 1st day of July, 2020." Opened https://grenadaparliament.gd/wp-content/uploads/2021/07/S.R.O.-44-of-2020-Consumer-Protection-Act-Commemcement-Order-2020.pdf (200, 223096 bytes) on 2026-11-03.
notes: Umbrella for environmental claims: it has no green-claims provision by name. The provisions that reach such claims are s. 56 (product labelling and trade descriptions) and s. 57 (disclosure of environmental facts affecting goods), plus the general misleading-conduct and unfair-practice parts. The Act as passed is stored dated its commencement; the Parliament site serves no consolidation, so the amendments of Act No. 5 of 2020 (gd-consumer-protection-amendment-2020) are a separate record. The commencement order (S.R.O. 44 of 2020) is cited in the evidence and not stored as its own entry. Language stored on 2026-11-03: en (English is the official language of legislation; the Parliament site serves no other language and no translation).

title: Non-Biodegradable Waste Control Act, 2018 (Act No. 9 of 2018)
citation: Non-Biodegradable Waste Control Act, 2018 (Act No. 9 of 2018), assented 1 August 2018
evidence: Act text, date line under the long title: "AN ACT to regulate the use of non-biodegradable products. [ August 10th, 2018 ]." The Act has no commencement clause (section 1 is the short title only); the bracketed date is read as the commencement date. Opened https://grenadaparliament.gd/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/Act-9-of-2018-Non-Biodegradable-Waste-Control.pdf (200, 373350 bytes) on 2026-11-03.
notes: Environmental statute (not a climate act): the Minister designates products by Order; import, manufacture and sale of a designated product are offences (ss. 4 to 6). Three Orders designate products (gd-nbwc-eps-order-2018, gd-nbwc-plastic-bags-order-2018, gd-nbwc-plastic-food-products-order-2019). Placed in F2 as the nearest environmental-framework family: it is a product-waste statute with no emissions duty. The date is the one the official text prints. Language stored on 2026-11-03: en (English is the official language of legislation; the Parliament site serves no other language and no translation).

title: Non-Biodegradable Waste Control (Expanded Polystyrene) Order, 2018 (S.R.O. 18 of 2018)

evidence: Order, header: "(Gazetted 14th September, 2018)". The Order has no commencement clause, so the gazette date is taken as in force (lookup policy). Its para 4 then sets the application dates of the Act: s. 4(1) "deemed to apply ... from the 1st day of September, 2018", s. 5(1) from 1 March 2019, s. 6(1) from 1 April 2019. Opened https://grenadaparliament.gd/wp-content/uploads/2021/08/S.R.O.-18-of-2018-Non-Biodegradable-Waste-Control-Expanded-Polystyrene-Order-1.pdf (200, 218336 bytes) on 2026-11-03.
notes: Implements gd-nbwc-act-2018: designates expanded polystyrene food containers as non-biodegradable products.
